failure_modes.recovery: do exactly what the error says — every refusal hands you the exact resend literals to copy.
failure_modes.when: the amount is a bare ambiguous number (dollars or cents?), exceeds the balance owed or a credit note's cap, names a different currency than the invoice, the invoice is a draft or cancelled, a type other than credit_note targets a 'paid' invoice or names reason_code or credit_outcome, or adjustment_type is dispute_settlement (reserved for the disputes flow)

failure_modes.recovery: Tell the owner: the error names the one step to run. Do not retry until it is done.
failure_modes.when: credit note numbering or the credit note fields are not set up in this environment yet (SIMPLER_SALES_NUMBERING_SERIES_UNMIGRATED or SIMPLER_SALES_CREDIT_NOTE_UNSEEDED)

failure_modes.recovery: Call invoice_list and retry with an id from the list.
failure_modes.when: invoice_id / invoice_number does not name an invoice in your tenant

failure_modes.recovery: The adjustment is parked for the account owner to approve in the Simpler UI.
failure_modes.when: an agent actor records an adjustment (shrinking the receivable book is human-approved)

preconditions: Money is integer CENTS ($15.00 → 1500) via amount_cents, or a decimal STRING via amount ("1500.00") — the server parses; never convert units yourself.

Adjustments act on ISSUED invoices. write_off and discount_post_issue need 'sent'; a credit_note works on 'sent' or 'paid'. A draft is edited or cancelled instead; a cancelled invoice owes nothing. A refund the business paid its customer outside Simpler is a credit_note with credit_outcome 'refunded_outside', not an expense.

A write_off, discount_post_issue or reduce_balance credit never exceeds the balance owed (total + debit notes − payments − prior adjustments). Every credit note is also capped at the total plus debit notes minus earlier credit notes, and a refunded_outside credit at the payments received minus earlier refunds. Writing off the whole remainder closes the receivable as the derived 'written_off' state — a write-off never makes it 'paid'. A credit covering the rest settles it to 'paid' only when at least one payment exists (paid means money arrived).

Give a reason — write-offs and credit notes are outcome records; the reason is what makes the record worth keeping. A credit_note also takes reason_code. To raise what an invoice is owed instead, use invoice_debit_note.

A credit_note's amount includes its tax. On an invoice with a tax scheme the tax inside it is worked out at the invoice's own rate, not today's (10.90 on a 9% GST invoice holds 0.90), and returned as tax_cents and net_cents; invoice_read tax_summary takes it off the output tax. On an invoice without a scheme tax_cents is 0. Send the amount the customer is credited, tax included.

description: [REQUIRES APPROVAL] Records a credit note, write-off or post-issue discount on an issued invoice. A credit_note is numbered from the credit note series, holds its tax at the invoice's rate and takes reason_code and credit_outcome: reduce_balance (default) lowers what is owed; refunded_outside records a refund the business made outside Simpler, moves no money and is how a 'paid' invoice gets one. write_off and discount_post_issue need a 'sent' invoice. Money is integer CENTS (amount_cents) or a decimal STRING (amount); caps: see preconditions. Refuses a draft, a cancelled invoice, an amount over its cap and dispute_settlement; each refusal names the fix. An agent's call parks for approval. NEXT: invoice_read.

amount.description: Money as a decimal STRING ("1500.00" = $1,500.00), parsed server-side. Use amount_cents for integer CENTS instead — never convert units yourself.

invoice_number.description: Alias of invoice_id — the invoice's own number (tenant-unique), resolved server-side.

partial.description: Confirms a deliberate PARTIAL write_off below the invoice's full remaining balance (checked only when adjustment_type is write_off) — resend the SAME call with partial:true; without it a below-remainder write_off refuses as a likely mis-carried amount.
